note_on_runtime: All variants trained on the SAME pool: data/evaluation/official/sentiment-test-v1 (train=1348, val=238) -- only input-text construction differs. Evaluated on the locked official test article_ids (n=283), each variant's own matching text transform. Production indobert_finetuned_v1 official macro-F1 on sentiment-test-v1 = 0.8096 (different, smaller/older training pool -- not a clean ablation comparison, informational reference only).

results.note: same formula as production (title + summary + short-fallback, 512 char truncation) -- this ablation's own local baseline (trained on the NEW 1348-row pool, unlike production which was trained on a different, older/smaller pool)

conclusion: None of the 3 input-text variants beat the current production formula (title+summary). title_only is statistically indistinguishable (delta -0.002, within noise). entity_prefix is measurably WORSE (delta -0.0355) -- prepending the ticker/company name hurts rather than helps, contrary to the 'target entity unclear' hypothesis. This is consistent with the R2 audit finding that label/model mismatch rate was NOT higher for multi-entity articles (4.5%) than single-entity articles (5.5%) -- entity ambiguity was never strongly supported as the main driver of the positive-class weakness. Recommendation: keep the current production input formula (title+summary) unchanged; input-text construction is not the lever that will meaningfully improve sentiment classification quality further. The remaining unexplored lever from the original diagnosis is full_text coverage (R7a/R7d), which requires a real scraping investment and was found infeasible to test cheaply with current data (0 negative examples among the 102 articles that have full_text).
